gap_description: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for BPPV canalithiasis — PINN-based modeling of otolith particle dynamics within the semicircular canal during benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. The canalithiasis theory posulates that detached otolith particles float in endolymph and obstruct cupula deflection during head movements. A PINN could learn the coupled ODE system describing particle position, velocity, cupula displacement, and endolymph viscosity from clinical positional test data (Dix-Hallpike, supine roll). This extends VOR-PINN-ODE success (Robinson model, clinical vHIT data, parameter recovery, Layer A=0.82) to BPPV domain. 0 meaningful papers exist across all permutations.
